subject_line: A Valley Girl Beowulf in The Daughter of Man
email_body:
Dear L.J.,

I came across the Colorado Review piece that described The Daughter of Man as a kind of "Valley Girl Beowulf," and I was struck that a University of Arkansas Press collection, a finalist for the Miller Williams Poetry Prize, could hold both registers at once. I would like to ask how that collision of epic and vernacular voice came about, and how it carries into your newer book, Battledore.

subject_line: Carrying Edimilson de Almeida Pereira's The Front into English
email_body:

email_body:

subject_line: Finding the voice of interiority in Sigrún Pálsdóttir
email_body:
Dear Lytton,

I read your Asymptote conversation about translating Sigrún Pálsdóttir's History. A Mess., and the way you described finding its voice of interiority. With nine books translated from Icelandic, including Ófeigur Sigurðsson's Öræfi for Deep Vellum, alongside your own Nightboat collections, I would like to ask how translation and your poetry feed each other. I was also glad to see a former Geneseo student, Rachel Britton, publish her own Icelandic translation in 2024.

subject_line: From the Harlingen citrus grove in Bang to How to Look Away
email_body:

I keep thinking about the family in Bang, living in a citrus grove outside Harlingen until a plane crash scatters them across the border. With How to Look Away now arriving, I would like to ask what changed in how you approach the border as a subject between the two books.

subject_line: What it means to be good, in These Trees, Those Leaves
email_body:
Dear Hayan,

I was drawn to how These Trees, Those Leaves, This Flower, That Fruit takes apart a deceptively simple question, what it means to be good, and to the way the title itself points at things one by one, as if naming were a moral act. subject_line: Querida Beth y las mujeres que construyen vida lejos de casa
email_body:
Hola Andrea:

Leí sobre Querida Beth, el libro con el que ganó el Premio Casa de América de Poesía Americana, y sobre cómo nace como homenaje en verso a su tía migrante y a las mujeres colombianas que construyen una vida lejos de casa. Me gustaría preguntarle por qué eligió dirigirse a Beth en el título, y qué cambió en su escritura al vivir y enseñar en El Paso, en la frontera, después de reunir su obra en Fervor de tierra.

subject_line: Apollo touring the Trojan War museums
email_body:

The title story of The Trojan War Museum, with Apollo wandering the Earth from one Trojan War museum to another and turning over the traumas of battle, has stayed with me, as has the plural "we" of the girls trapped in the rubble in "The History of Girls."
